story_text.value:
Hi HN. GIFUP was an avatar and glitter generator I ran from 2007; it made about 1.3M animations before the web moved on. This year I rebuilt the domain as a set of GIF tools where the encoding happens in the tab via ffmpeg.wasm: video to GIF, compress, resize, crop, captions, GIF to MP4, plus presets that fit Discord, Slack, Twitch and WhatsApp limits.

Nothing is uploaded. The file is read from disk, FFmpeg runs in WebAssembly, and the result is handed back as a blob. The engine is about 10 MB compressed, fetched once and cached. The core is single-threaded because the threaded build needs COOP/COEP headers, so a 10-second 720p clip takes a few seconds rather than a fraction of one. No size caps, no queue, no account.

Two optional server features: "Get a link" hosts a finished file if you want to paste it in a forum, and a WhatsApp sticker page can deliver a sticker to your phone. Both are off until you press the button.

The glue code on the page is plain JS; the FFmpeg build is the unmodified @ffmpeg/core 0.12.6 (GPL, libx264 and libx265 included). I would like to hear where it breaks, especially on Safari, and which tool you are missing.

title.value: Show HN: Gifup – GIF tools that run in the browser (ffmpeg.wasm)

story_text.value:
Hey HN, I've been building Sectr, a backend-as-a-service for making it easy(ier) to develop and deploy AI agents. Deploying agents requires non-trivial systems design work. Consider a support agent: how do you stream messages to your frontend, how/where do you persist messages for frontend fetching later (or for auditing), and when the agent wants to issue a refund, do you spin-down the compute infra while it's waiting on human approval? Sectr aims to be the serverless abstraction and platform to provide these systems for you.

No sign-up needed to try using the dev server:

  curl -fsSL https://sectr.dev/install.sh | sh # Install CLI
  sectr init my-agent && cd my-agent # Starter code
  sectr dev # Dev server, with UI to test chatting
Sectr provides:

- Streaming of every token, tool call and event, and persistence so they can be loaded fresh later.

- Scaling up, and down to zero when the agent needs to wait, and resumption right to the suspended agent's state.

- Human approved tools automatically use Sectr's suspension and resumption capabilities, no code needed from you.

- AG-UI endpoint for any deployed agent so you can trivially hook up your frontend

- Local dev server experience, so you can rapidly debug and iterate on your agent's behavior

At the core, you can deploy any container image to Sectr as long as it implements a certain shaped HTTP endpoint. In practice, currently Sectr provides adapters to let you deploy your existing OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, or Pydantic AI agents, with only 2 new lines of code:

  app = AgentApp(name="support")
  app.add_route("/chat", openai_agents(agent))
Certainly the hardest part of building Sectr was getting the resumption logic to be correct and invisible, across the Program State x Model Provider x Agent Framework matrix. For example, an earlier bug was when a model replied with text plus a tool call, Sectr would resume that as two separate messages, instead of one message with a text and tool part. This works, but breaks prompt caching (and might subtly change model behavior).

Sectr is free during the beta (and can be tried locally without sign-up); I mainly want feedback, especially on dev & deployment experiences, any bugs, and what features would excite you.

Introductory video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H-y3wynkKc0

Docs: https://docs.sectr.dev

title.value: Show HN: Sectr – Serverless backend platform for easy deployment of AI agents

story_text.value:
Hey HN, I recently published a project for running self hosted, highly available ingress for your infrastructure: authoritative DNS for your own domain, load balancers and network mesh, to expose your web apps. It started over a year ago as side project to handle several websites for clients and other side projects, and finished as the replacement cert-manager, external-dns and ingress that works without k8s, and is independent from single cloud/vps provider.

It ended up as the HA platform, able to manage dozens of load balancers with TLS termination (and Let's Encrypt integration), DNS servers and full redundant mesh. The design goal from the beginning was to prepare a tool with minimized risk of single point of failure and independent from single hosting.

It is running all my home lab, nextcloud, gitlab and production websites for clients for the few last months.

Quick links for those who want to test: https://dinemic.com - project page https://console.dinemic.com - hosted control plane, if you want to test it with your own vps and domain, without setting up whole stack https://gitlab.cloudover.io/dinemic/docs - project documentation

In high availability section of documentation you will also find concepts and design of its components and sample analysis of downtime when things go wrong with your infra.

It is AGPL, so you can host also at your own. Self hosted version covers all functionality, with API and command line tools.

title.value: Show HN: Dinemic – self-hosted ingress across multiple providers (DNS, LB, TLS)
